subject: Evaluation success metrics and hotfix SLA — ChipWise POC
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@chipwise.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation success metrics and hotfix SLA — ChipWise POC

Hi Sam / ChipWise team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

High-level goal for POC (2 weeks): validate Redwood inference runtime for ChipWise interactive search use case with production-like traffic and acceptance criteria below.

Agreed acceptance criteria (please confirm or flag changes):
- Functional: accuracy/parity: top-3 rerank precision >= 0.78 on your eval set (we'll run your 2k sample).
- Performance: 95th perc latency <= 350ms for single-query web traffic pattern; median < 120ms.
- Reliability: <1% failed requests over a rolling 24h window during the test runs.
- Cost/throughput: maintain target cost per 1k queries within the budget you shared (we'll map exact numbers once we have the dataset).
- Security/compliance: redaction and KMS proof-of-concept for secrets access (Laura's team will validate).

Immediate asks for ChipWise to unblock the setup:
1) Share the 2k eval sample (anonymized) and a short doc listing expected edge cases by Wed EOD PT.
2) Approve the Data Access Addendum we sent (doc link below) so we can provision test keys.
3) Confirm if you want us to enable request-level logs (we suggested a whitelisted view) — need sign-off for sample logs by Thu.

Internal owners / commitments from Redwood:
- Marcus Lin: runtime lead — will coordinate the initial infra build and performance baseline.
- Priyom Das: onboarding/QA — will validate dataset ingestion and eval harness.
- Neha (me): customer point of contact — coordinate comms and acceptance sign-off.

Risk note: on the call we flagged the KV-cache race we saw in a previous pilot — Marcus and I agreed to hold a short tech spike if we see instability. Proposed hotfix SLA: commit to a P1 patch within 72 hours of reproduction during the POC window; P2 within 5 business days. Please confirm this cadence works for ChipWise.

Attached: chipwise_acceptance_matrix.xlsx (draft), chipwise_test_plan_v1.pdf
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_chipwise-poc-docs

Next steps: Sam — can you confirm the eval sample delivery and whether Laura's team requires a separate NDA for logs? If those are green, we'll schedule infra provisioning for Thu morning.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

---

From: Sam Reynolds <sam@chipwise.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Finch <security@chipwise.io>, ChipWise Procurement <procure@getchipwise.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success metrics and hotfix SLA — ChipWise POC

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. All good directionally, a few clarifications from our side: 

1) Eval sample: we'll deliver the anonymized 2k CSV by Tue 17:00 PT. It will include a column with expected labels and a brief notes column for edge-case examples.

2) Latency target: the 95th <= 350ms is acceptable, but our product team also asked for a 99th cap for heavy queries — can Redwood provide a short note on fallback behavior if 99th spikes during a run? A temporary fallback to a smaller model is acceptable if documented.

3) Security: Laura asked that KMS integration evidence be provided before any request-level logs are shared. She also asked whether logs can be delivered to an S3 bucket with access controls (we can provide a temporary bucket).

4) Hotfix SLA: the 72-hour commit for P1 sounds reasonable, but procurement will want that in the SOW if a P1 impacts availability during the paid trial.

Attached: chipwise_internal_test_plan_comments.pdf (inline comments).

One ask on blockers: our SRE mentioned a past incident where model cache misses produced 500s under load — that would be a showstopper for us. Would you call that a P1? If so, please outline the immediate mitigation path we can expect while a patch is prepared.

I'll loop in procurement after we confirm the data access agreement.

—Sam
Head of Product | ChipWise
sam@chipwise.io

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sam Reynolds <sam@chipwise.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success metrics and hotfix SLA — ChipWise POC

Thanks — logging a concise risk/mitigation table and owners so we have clear escalation paths during the POC. I'm putting this in writing so procurement / legal can see commitments.

Risk / Likelihood / Severity / Owner / Mitigation / ETA for mitigation
1) Persistent 500s from KV-cache race (seen in internal pilot) / medium / P1 (availability) / Marcus Lin / Immediate mitigation: enable cold-cache serialization + force-prefetch for session keyspace; temporary routing to a smaller model variant if errors spike. ETA to deploy mitigation as a config flip: 4 hours once we have access to repro traffic. Permanent fix (code-level) ETA: 72 hours from reproduction.

2) KMS integration proof / low-med / P2 (security gating) / Priyom Das / Provide KMS audit logs and config screenshots, plus a short runbook for key rotation. ETA: 2 business days to produce artifacts once access is granted.

3) 99th percentile latency spikes under heavy concurrent bursts / medium / P1/P2 depending on impact / Marcus Lin / Mitigation: controlled throttling + adaptive batching thresholds during test runs; fallback to smaller model for degraded tail latency. ETA for tuning: baseline tests 24 hours, quick config change immediate.

4) Data access/legal delays / low / P2 / Neha Kapoor / Work with ChipWise procurement to prioritize the Data Addendum. Neha to escalate to Lauren for expedited approvals if needed.

Hotfix / SLA commitments we can make (subject to SOW language):
- P1 (availability impacting error >=0.5% request failure or 5+ min sustained 5xx): commit to an engineering owner on-call and a code-level patch or configuration mitigation committed in 72 hours.
- P2 (degraded latency / non-blocking correctness regressions): commit to fix within 5 business days.

Escalation contacts (POC window):
- Level 1 (on-call runtime): marcus.lin@redwood.com (Slack: @marcus-runtime)
- Level 2 (ops lead): priyom.das@redwood.com
- Executive escalation: lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Interim mitigations we'll enable immediately during the first smoke run (Thu):
- Prefix/KV-cache safety flags (config flip).
- Disable non-essential tracing to reduce tail latency.
- Route 10% of traffic to smaller model as canary if tail latency increases past threshold.

I'll patch a short hotfix diff (hotfix_patch_diff.txt) and attach — that contains the config safety guard. Neha — please confirm we can start the runtime change window Thu 07:00 PT. Sam — if ChipWise can provide repro traffic or a sample synthetic load, we'll use it to validate mitigations before the run.

Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Sam Reynolds <sam@chipwise.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700

Appreciate the clear remediation plan. ChipWise agrees to the proposed hotfix cadence (72h for P1) provided it's reflected in the SOW. Procurement will draft a short SOW addendum for trial-specific remediation SLAs.

Next steps we will take this week:
- Deliver anonymized 2k eval CSV Tue 17:00 PT (Sam) — DONE (uploaded to your Drive).
- Laura will confirm KMS artifact requirements by EOD Thu and provide a temporary S3 bucket for logs if approved.
- ChipWise SRE will generate a 30-min synthetic load by Wed 18:00 PT and share a repro trace for the KV-cache scenario if it reproduces.

We approve the runtime config flip Thu 07:00 PT — thanks Marcus for the quick mitigation plan. Please keep comms tight: if you flip the config, notify security and procurement.

Sam
Head of Product | ChipWise
